title: Docs: Build a manual page only when its program is built
description:
The manual pages are added to the build unconditionally, so a build
configured without a program still generates, installs and packages
that program's page.

The default configuration shows it. BUILD_stratoshark is OFF by
default, yet stratoshark(1), strato(1), falcodump(1), sshdig(1) and
dumpcalls(1) are built and installed anyway, along with the Stratoshark
release notes, documenting programs that were never compiled. The same
goes for anything else switched off: randpktdump(1) survives
-DBUILD_randpktdump=OFF, and etwdump(1) is installed on every platform,
though the program it describes is built only on Windows.

Guard each page on the option that decides whether its program is
built, which is what dpauxmon, sdjournal and mmdbresolve already do a
few lines further down. Extend the same to the HTML pages in
DOC_FILES, where falcodump and dumpcalls were already guarded and the
rest were not, and to the Stratoshark release notes.

Pages for things that are always built - wireshark, tshark, capinfos,
captype, dumpcap, editcap, mergecap, randpkt, rawshark, reordercap,
sharkd, text2pcap and the section 4 pages - stay unconditional.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 5c40ee64 - Docs: Build a manual page only when its program is built
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/26425/diffs?diff_id=2012591899&start_sha=69917521506157f81aac9140aa945f8bfc443ae3)

> Pages for things that are always built - wireshark, tshark, capinfos, captype, dumpcap, editcap, mergecap, randpkt, rawshark, reordercap, sharkd, text2pcap and the section 4 pages - stay unconditional.

Those are always built *by default*, but the user can disable them if they choose, e.g. if you're building for a platform that can't run GUI applications locally and you don't care about building a version that can use X11-over-the-wire, you can disable Wireshark.

But avoiding building man pages for *any* program that can be disabled can be left to a later change.

The online man pages at https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/ are currently built on my local machine running macOS, although moving that to *.gitlab-ci.yml* is on my to-do list. In either case this would make that part of the release process tricky.
One option might be to add an "install" parameter to ADD_MAN_PAGE so that we could build them unconditionally and install them conditionally.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/26425/diffs?diff_id=2022557274&start_sha=5c40ee645c5a6964c5a13530d15cfd4155d4a9c0#f7878a6f3ed0ffa338c24bedcb1a7cb9b670a877_80_48)

Done — I went with your suggestion. ADD_MAN_PAGE now takes a third argument, the install condition: every page is still generated unconditionally (all of them are added to the manpages/docs targets), and only installation and packaging are gated on that condition.

So an ordinary configure — the kind that produces the online man pages at wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/ — still builds the complete set, whether that's your macOS box today or .gitlab-ci.yml later. Nothing about the release process changes; only make install/packaging now ships a subset.

I verified it against a default build (BUILD_stratoshark and friends off): stratoshark(1), strato(1), idl2wrs(1) etc. are still generated in the build tree, but no longer land in the install manifest.

The always-built programs (wireshark, tshark, …) keep installing their pages unconditionally for now; gating those on their own BUILD_* options can be a later change, per @guyharris's note.

commits_data.title: Docs: Generate every manual page, install only the ones built
commits_data.message:
Docs: Generate every manual page, install only the ones built

The manual pages were added to the build unconditionally, so a build
configured without a program still installed and packaged that program's
page. A default build shows it: with BUILD_stratoshark off, stratoshark(1),
strato(1) and the Stratoshark release notes were installed anyway, and the
same held for anything switched off - randpktdump(1) survived
-DBUILD_randpktdump=OFF, and etwdump(1) was installed off Windows.

Simply guarding each page on its build option would stop generating it, but
the online manual pages at https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/ are
built from an ordinary configure, so a page that is no longer generated
would drop off the website.

Keep generating every page, then, and gate only installation. ADD_MAN_PAGE
takes a third argument, the install condition: the page is always added to
the build - and to the manpages and docs targets - but installed and
packaged only when that argument is true, following the same conditions
extcap/CMakeLists.txt builds each program under. The same split is applied
to the HTML pages in DOC_FILES and to the Stratoshark release notes.

Pages for things that are always built stay installed unconditionally;
gating those on their own BUILD_* options can be a later change.

sshdig moves to the stratoshark package in the Debian packaging. It is a
Stratoshark extcap, installed into STRATOSHARK_EXTCAP_INSTALL_LIBDIR and
shipped with stratoshark, but its manual page was listed in
wireshark-common - already wrong, as a default build has no sshdig binary
in that package.
